messages.author: 929e733ff7821ad3
messages.subject: multi-core setting in R-INLA
parts:
Dear all,

I have check some old post about setting multi-core running for INLA. Below is the code I used to run:

fit <- inla(f3, 
                  family = "binomial",
                  lincomb = mylincomb,
                  data = inla.stack.data(mystack),
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, openmp.strategy="huge"),
                  control.predictor = list(
                    A = inla.stack.A(mystack)),
                  control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"), 
                  verbose=TRUE
)

I have a large data set of 181362 rows, with 11 covariates, a rw2 function and a spde. 

I am running the script on a super computer with 72 cores and 400GB internal memory. 

however, I dont see that I am runing on multi-cores, even after many hours so far. I am wondering whether there are part of the R-INLA procedure that are not able to run on multi-core (like an initialization step) that might take hours? Or if multi-core works, it should immediately start? (then in this case, my super computer does not allow multi-core)

Thanks

Chun Chen

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] multi-core setting in R-INLA
parts:
Hi,

check out

inla.pardiso()

you might need an upgrade if you have an old version.

strategy = 'adaptive' is the new and better choice than 'gaussian'
(same speed...)

let me know.

H

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: multi-core setting in R-INLA
parts:
Unless you're using the new PARDISO sparse library, this could happen,
as its simply get to large for one core. using the 'pardiso.parallel'
should resolve this issue; see inla.pardiso()

this feature is experimental for the moment and require a license,
which is free for academic work.

H
